core_obligations: Existence of the pushout (proof lines 5130-5134): the author sets the pushout equal to the cokernel of the map (g, -f) from the first filtered object into the direct sum of the third and second, notes that this cokernel exists by the cited lemma, and identifies it as the pushout through the cited example.

Strictness (proof lines 5135-5141): the filtration step of the pushout is the image of the corresponding steps of the two summands, from which the author computes the preimage of that step under the induced map and shows that it is the image of the corresponding step of the second object together with the previous step of the third, which is exactly strictness.
proof_roadmap: Build the pushout as the cokernel of the difference map into the direct sum.
Identify it as a pushout by the standard example.
Compute the filtration steps of the pushout and the preimage along the induced map to get strictness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the category of filtered objects of an abelian category admits pushouts, constructed as the cokernel of the difference of the two given maps, and that the induced map from the second object is strict whenever the first given map is (statement lines 5115-5128). The proof is a complete argument: the pushout is exhibited as a cokernel, whose existence is supplied by a named lemma, and identified through a named example (proof lines 5130-5134); the filtration step of the pushout is described as an image and the preimage along the induced map is computed to be the displayed sum, which is strictness (proof lines 5135-5141). The non-formal content is the computation of the filtration step of the pushout. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
